title: General Knowledge
description: Everyday world knowledge: geography, science, history and culture.

questions.text: What is the capital of Azerbaijan?
questions.explanation: Baku is the capital and largest city of Azerbaijan.

questions.text: Which is the largest planet in the Solar System?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is more massive than all the other planets combined.

questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: Au comes from the Latin word 'aurum'.

questions.text: Who wrote the play 'Hamlet'?
questions.explanation: Hamlet was written by William Shakespeare around 1600.

questions.text: How many continents are there on Earth?
questions.explanation: The usual model counts seven continents.

questions.text: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean covers about a third of the Earth's surface.

questions.text: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100 °C (212 °F) at standard sea-level pressure.

questions.text: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Iron oxide on its surface gives Mars a reddish colour.

questions.text: Which is the longest river in Europe?
questions.explanation: The Volga is about 3,500 km long.

questions.text: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa in the early 1500s.

questions.text: What is the hardest natural substance?
questions.explanation: Diamond is the hardest naturally occurring material.

questions.text: In which year did World War II end?
questions.explanation: World War II ended in 1945.

questions.text: Which is the largest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Russia covers more than 17 million square kilometres.

questions.text: Which gas do plants absorb for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen.

questions.text: What is the approximate speed of light?
questions.explanation: Light travels at about 300,000 km per second in a vacuum.

questions.text: Who developed the theory of relativity?
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein published the theory of relativity in the early 20th century.

questions.text: What is the smallest prime number?
questions.explanation: 2 is the smallest prime and the only even prime.

questions.text: What is the currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: Japan uses the yen.

questions.text: How many bones does an adult human body have?
questions.explanation: An adult has 206 bones.

questions.text: Which organ pumps blood through the human body?
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood through the circulatory system.

questions.text: What is the highest mountain above sea level?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest rises about 8,849 m above sea level.

questions.text: Which language has the most native speakers?
questions.explanation: Mandarin Chinese has the most native speakers.

questions.text: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969.

questions.text: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra, not Sydney, is the capital of Australia.

questions.text: Which continent has no permanent population?
questions.explanation: Antarctica has only temporary research station staff.

questions.text: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun.

questions.text: Which substance has the chemical formula H2O?
questions.explanation: H2O is two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom: water.

questions.text: Who is usually credited with inventing the telephone?
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell received the first telephone patent in 1876.

questions.text: How many players does one football (soccer) team have on the pitch?
questions.explanation: Each team plays with eleven players, including the goalkeeper.

questions.text: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest what?
questions.explanation: The Caspian Sea is the largest enclosed inland body of water.
